title: Build a confidence interval step by step
objectives: Compute the standard error for a known population standard deviation.
Build a two-sided confidence interval and interpret it correctly.

sources.title: Original arithmetic fixture, independently recomputed in the harness tests

slides.title: Estimate, then quantify uncertainty
slides.body: For a random independent sample from a normal population with known population standard deviation, use mean ± z × sigma / square root of n. This example supplies z = 1.96 for a 95% two-sided interval.
slides.retrieval_prompt: Name the estimate, the measure of uncertainty and the assumptions before calculating.

exercises.statement: A random sample of 64 independent measurements has mean 100 g. The normal population has known standard deviation 16 g. Use z = 1.96 to construct the 95% confidence interval.
exercises.translation: Find the uncertainty of the sample mean, scale it by the supplied critical value, then go that distance below and above the mean.
exercises.interpretation: The interval is [96.08 g, 103.92 g]. Across repeated samples under these assumptions, about 95% of intervals made by this procedure cover the fixed population mean.

steps.prompt: Compute the standard error, 16 / sqrt(64), in grams.
hints: Calculate the square root before dividing.
steps.misconception: Dividing by n instead of its square root understates uncertainty.

steps.prompt: Compute the margin of error, 1.96 × 2, in grams.
hints: Multiply the critical value by the standard error.
steps.misconception: The standard error alone is not the 95% margin of error.

steps.prompt: Compute the lower endpoint, 100 − 3.92, in grams.
hints: Move below the sample mean by one margin of error.
steps.misconception: Moving up gives the upper endpoint, not the lower one.
